evidenceClass: Installed pinned Babylon library source and current Web implementation; no original2016 renderer equivalence claim

sections.purpose: Public reparent calls native cached enabled synchronization
isEnabled is two cached booleans; own/effective public notifications
Public getNodes includes render and non-render nodes
Constructor-default provider is an instance arrow over current scene.meshes
Mesh add notification deferred; remove notification synchronous
Public add supports insertFirst and returns removal handle

facts: Node.isEnabled is not a recursive per-query ancestor walk; it reads cached own/parent booleans.
setEnabled/reparent synchronizes descendants and emits effective notifications, including inherited changes.
Scene default getActiveMeshCandidates is a per-instance arrow. Function names or a nonexistent prototype function do not prove default identity.
The game captures that provider directly after new Scene and opts into public Scene-managed membership and stock Node enabled semantics.
Mesh add is notified later, so data identity/length checks complement public membership events before an indexed result.
Own/effective notification turns may reenter during native descendant propagation; those queries retain the previous literal filter until the next microtask.
Custom/unknown providers, incompatible runtime, provider shape changes, duplicate candidate identities and unsupported Node methods use the literal original filter.
boundaries: Silent same-array same-length scene.meshes writes bypassing public Scene membership are outside the explicit production contract.
Private Node cache writes and unregistered/custom enabled-observable implementations are not indexed.
The inserted-first observer guard is owned by the controlled scene; arbitrary later custom insertFirst callbacks that deliberately preempt it are outside that production ownership contract.
No isReady, culling, LOD, geometry, visibility or material count is changed. Candidate iteration still keeps original provider order.
Only operation counters and semantics are unit-tested here. Runtime FPS/CPU improvements require the separate actual-browser comparison.
